parameters.customBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ currentFeedUrl: $json.currentFeedUrl || undefined, currentFeedText: $json.currentFeedText || undefined, previousFeedUrl: $json.previousFeedUrl || undefined, previousFeedText: $json.previousFeedText || undefined, useStoredBaseline: $json.useStoredBaseline, baselineName: $json.baselineName, baselineStoreId: $json.baselineStoreId || undefined, lockQueueId: $json.lockQueueId || undefined, maxItems: 1000 }) }}

parameters.content:
Before activation, replace currentFeedUrl with a supplier feed you are authorized to process. Leave previousFeedUrl and previousFeedText empty. The Actor auto-detects common key, price, availability, and title columns; this template does not send explicit column overrides.

This workflow uses the Actor stored baseline. The first run saves a baseline and returns no change rows, so no email is sent. Later daily runs compare the current feed and send one plain-text summary only when changed rows exist. Each email includes up to 50 item keys/titles and price or availability changes; currency is shown when the feed supplies it. Open the Actor run history for the full dataset.

Use a unique baselineName for each supplier. baselineStoreId and lockQueueId are optional and must be set together. For restricted Apify run tokens, create/select the matching baseline store and per-baseline lock queue, then set both IDs. The lock queue name is derived from baselineName; see the README for the exact rule. The Actor requests READ and WRITE for the selected resources. The name-based path with blank IDs was not covered by this test; run a manual seed check before relying on it.

Configure the email sender, recipient, and SMTP credential. The schedule is set to 08:00 UTC and is inactive until you activate the workflow. Change the workflow timezone before activation if needed.

Restricted Apify token setup: set baselineStoreId to your authorized key-value store ID and lockQueueId to your authorized request queue ID. For the default baselineName supplier-one, the queue must be named catalog-feed-diff-lock-2888b138787414f7723a47cf. This exact ID-based restricted-token path was tested; blank-ID/name-based restricted-token setup was not.
